Why Starship

The point of Starship is not that it is the biggest rocket.
It is that mass to orbit stops being a one-way ticket.

@elonmusk 
“It's the first rocket design that is capable of full and rapid reusability.”

Translation: every other orbital rocket is still a disposable truck. Starship is built so the truck comes home and goes again. Refill is the next chapter. Reuse is the breakthrough.

1. Falcon Heavy: ~64 t to LEO (expendable)
2. Starship V3: >100 t to LEO reusable (SpaceX’s stated target)
3. You cannot make enough rockets unless you can refly them
4. Flight 13: Ship came home intact after entry

You cannot become multiplanetary on expendable trucks.

He says the whole industry is about to learn a hard lesson in hardware.

tweets.text: Extending consciousness beyond Earth, ultimately to the stars, is a fundamentally good goal

quoted.text:
SpaceX’s road to making humanity multiplanetary is really incredible when you see the milestones together

- 2008 → Falcon 1 becomes the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit
- 2010 → Falcon 9 completes its first flight
- 2012 → Dragon becomes the first private spacecraft to visit the ISS
- 2015 → Falcon 9 lands on land for the first time
- 2016 → First Falcon 9 droneship landing
- 2017 → First Falcon 9 booster reflight
- 2018 → Falcon Heavy launches for the first time
- 2020 → SpaceX returns human spaceflight to America
- 2021 → Starship SN15 completes a successful high-altitude flight and landing
- 2021 → Inspiration4 becomes the first all-civilian crew to orbit
- 2022 → Starship and Super Heavy become a full stack
- 2023 → First integrated Starship flight
- 2024 → Super Heavy gets caught by the launch tower for the first time
- 2025 → A Super Heavy booster flies for a second time
- 2026 → Starship V3 and Raptor 3 take flight

18 years of relentless iteration.

Falcon 1 → Falcon 9 → Dragon → Falcon Heavy → Starship.

Each milestone solved another piece of the puzzle

And the destination has stayed the same from the beginning:

Make life multiplanetary
